summary: Dali is best for slower, open-air travel shaped by mountain-and-lake light, old-town texture, and generous room for wandering.
transport_notes: Dali works best when old town, lakeside, and outlying scenic areas are not all forced into the same dense day.
Slower pacing matters here; solo and reflective trips benefit from leaving time between major stops.
Short car or local transport hops are useful, but plans should still keep one clear geographic focus per day.

budget_notes.low: Focus on walking, old-town browsing, lake views, and simple local meals.
budget_notes.medium: Mix one atmospheric old-town stretch, one scenic lake or village stop, and one slow dining moment each day.
budget_notes.high: Allow more open time, softer boutique pacing, and stronger landscape-led meal choices.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans should make Dali feel relaxed, photogenic, and backpacker-friendly without overspending.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize freedom, mountain-lake stillness, personal rhythm, and contemplative wandering.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should lean into lakeside light, old-town intimacy, and soft scenic transitions.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should keep movement easy, avoid overlong scenic detours, and favor calm open spaces.
